To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the best approach for Spoken Web Searching is to build a GUM/HMM for each of the queries using a KLT transform on the log-phones of the queries, (2) a GMM/HUM is a good model for representing the queries, (3) the best features are the log-phones, (4) the best acoustic modeling approach is the KLT, and (5) the best acoustic keyword spotting system is the GMM/HMM.
a GMM/HMT-based approach performs the best, and that applying a Kar-hunen-Loève transform on query posteriors improves the performance.

(1) applying the KLT to the query log-phones posteriors is the key to improve performance and (2) the best results are achieved when the GMMs/HMMs for each query are trained on a large amount of data, i.e. the entire query log.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a robust and efficient spoken query recognition system that is capable of dealing with the problems of noisy environments and the large vocabulary of the spoken web search task.
the design and development of an automatic speech recognition (ASR) system that will enable the use of spoken queries to retrieve relevant documents from the Web.
the development and evaluation of spoken query recognition techniques for the Spoken Web search task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best performing approach is the one which combines both a query-dependent GMM/HMM and a query-independent GMM/HMM, with a subsequent AKWS, which is the approach we call the "hybrid" approach.
the AKWS approach outperforms the DTW approach, but the latter is more robust to noise and speaker variability, which are the two main problems of the AKWS system.
the Spoken Web Task is not a solved problem yet, but the AKWS approach is a promising way to solve it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to achieve a 0.4% relative improvement in performance by using a GMM/HMT model for the query and a subsequent keyword spotting system.
we are still far away from the ideal solution, but that we have a good understanding of the problem.
a good AKWS system is a key component for spoken web search.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a query-dependent GMM/HMM to perform AKWS is a promising direction to pursue.
a query-based system performs better than a system based on a generic language model.
AKWS can be used for spoken query search in the Spoken Web domain.
